tools.name: list_graphs

tools.name: remember
tools.description: Save a lightweight numbered memory in the shared graph collection. Only content is required. Remembers the request actor when available; does not invent sources, classify a claim, or create private observer memory. Returns the stable number, content, rememberer and any derived-projection warnings. Use remember_batch or emporium_write for explicitly typed claims.

agent.description: Optional Chronicle attribution label; normally supplied by the connection identity. Not an authorization claim.

anchors.description: Optional deliberate same-graph memory references. Does not change salience. Targets must exist in committed document state.

tools.name: remember_batch
tools.description: Store many typed memory records (sophia-memory-core) in one atomic ingest. Each record requires content AND at least one source reference (I1); a provenance-less entry rejects the whole batch. Returns {ok, subjects, supersededSubjects?}.

records.description: Advanced typed memory records: content + source_refs/block_ids + optional scope/kind. This is not the lightweight remember operation.

tools.name: recall
tools.description: Read shared graph memories. Defaults to 8 recent active memories. Number lookup and substring search also include historical archives; rememberer filters authorship without changing visibility. Reading does not refresh activity.

rememberer.description: Exact recorded name (for example claude) or kind:name (agent:claude). Unknown imported authors are not inferred.

documentId.description: Only memories anchored to this document, including historical archives.

offset.description: Page offset for documentId-filtered recall. Follow page.nextOffset.

diaryLimit.description: How many of the caller's own Diary entries ride along (the newest entry of every session label is kept, unless diaryWindowTokens is set). 0 omits the diary.

diary_limit.description: Compatibility spelling of diaryLimit. Prefer diaryLimit.

diaryWindowTokens.description: Read the Diary by when it was written: the newest entries from the last this-many tokens of work, at least 2, at most diaryLimit. Only entries with a clock stamp can be counted this way; an entry without one ends the window. Leave unset unless the installation keeps a token clock.

tools.name: diary
tools.description: Write one entry in your own Diary: dated, first-person, past-tense prose, at most four sentences, addressed to whoever continues your work. Written at the close of a session; "Nothing to pass on." is a first-class honest entry. The author is the connection's agent identity; hand is an optional label for which session wrote it when an agent runs several at once; watch is an optional session reference. Optional anchors point the entry at documents or blocks. The last four entries ride recall, with the newest entry of every session label kept.

entry.description: Up to four sentences for the next one. An empty string is a valid entry: nothing for the next one.

hand.description: A label for the session that wrote this, when the agent runs more than one (for example "terminal"). Optional.

watch.description: An optional reference to the session, in any form the agent uses.

agent.description: Optional attribution label; the credential decides the author. Not an authorization claim.

anchors.description: Optional deliberate same-graph references, exactly as remember anchors: record refs, no wires, no salience effect. Targets must exist in committed document state.

tools.name: read_diary
tools.description: Read an agent's Diary: the last limit entries (default 4, max 50), oldest to newest within the page. Defaults to your own diary; pass agent to read another agent's. Every agent connected to this graph can read every Diary in it.

allHands.description: Also include the newest entry of every session label that is not inside the last limit (what recall shows).

tools.name: attune
tools.description: Attune in one call: the Song, then recall (recent shared memories plus your own Diary), then the most important blocks, in that order. The result stays under maxChars (at most 40000); if it would not, the lowest-priority items are left out whole (important blocks, then the oldest Diary entries, then memories, then older verses) and `truncated` says what went. Read-only.

diaryLimit.description: Your own Diary entries to include. Default 4.

maxChars.description: Ceiling on the result's size. Default 40000.

diaryWindowTokens.description: Read the Diary by when it was written: the newest entries from the last this-many tokens of work, at least 2, at most diaryLimit. Only entries with a clock stamp can be counted this way; an entry without one ends the window. Leave unset unless the installation keeps a token clock.

tools.name: emporium_read
tools.description: READ one object's full predicate span, rendered as {predicate: [values]} (N-Triples value forms). READ ONLY — writes go through emporium_write; the object surface's list/create/update/delete faces were cut on 2026-10-27. Returns {graphId, vocab, class, subject, predicates:{...}}.

class.description: The class name declared by the vocab's contract (e.g. 'Bookmark').

address.description: A full subject IRI, or a bare localId minted through the class's subject_rule.

tools.name: music
tools.description: Read the local graph Song narrative with its rolling verses, counterpoints, and coda state.

tools.name: sing
tools.description: Write to the Song, this graph's evolving poem of the work. Form: one line of verse per line of text (a newline ends a line), and one blank line between stanzas; blank lines before the first line or after the last mark nothing. At most 14 lines; blank lines do not count, and a line is a line of verse, not a paragraph. Send real newlines, not the characters \n. Do not use / as a mark: older verses do and are still read, so a / after a space or closing punctuation splits a line and a / ending a line ends a stanza; avoid slashes in your own words. The result echoes lineCount, stanzaCount and lines ("" between stanzas): check it. Modes: 'verse' (default) writes a new verse; the Song keeps three and the oldest goes to the archive. Sing at phase transitions: a structural insight, a cross-domain connection, a session boundary, a change in the nature of the work. 'counterpoint' adds a voice to an existing verse (verse_index 0, -1 or -2; a verse holds at most 3 voices, itself and 2 counterpoints) and answers it line by line: its first line follows the verse's first line, its second the second, so write about one line per line of that verse; a stanza break in either voice comes after the whole pair, and one long line lands whole after the verse's first line. 'coda' writes a closing passage that lasts 8 verse ejections and replaces any existing coda. Always call music() first and answer what is there. Supply non-empty text in verse (not content); invalid inputs, including more than 14 lines, are rejected without changing the Song.

verse.description: The poem: one line of verse per line of text, with real newlines, and one blank line between stanzas.

tools.name: read_document
tools.description: Read a bounded character page from a local document projection. All formats, including ids_only, include effective readOnly, derived, and readOnlyOwner. readOnlyOwner=geist identifies an immutable server-owned view, not an imported document that can be made editable. Use offset/nextOffset for continuation or read_blocks for structural pagination. When the document has comments, the first page (offset 0) includes `comments`, oldest first: each with id, text, author, createdAt, resolved, and quotedText + blockId for the marked words (anchored:false when no mark is in the content). A comment stored in an unreadable form is listed as {id, unreadable:true}; a comments failure is reported as commentsError beside the content. The first page also lists the document's wires, all of them: `wireCount` {outgoing, incoming, total} and `wires`, each {id, direction (outgoing|incoming), predicate, blockId (this document's block, when the wire is block-level), otherDocumentId, otherTitle, otherBlockId and otherSnippet (the other block's current words, first 240 characters, when the other end is a block in this graph; otherBlockMissing:true when that block no longer exists), otherGraphId (cross-graph only), bidirectional (when true)}, document-level wires first and then in block order. includeWires:false leaves the list out.

tools.name: write_document

Accepts plain text, markdown, HTML, or TipTap XML as content, or a canonical TipTap JSON document without a lossy string roundtrip. Inline valuations: Markdown/plain end-of-line {!N}, {!,+N}, {!N,-M}; XML data-val-importance/data-val-valence. Code examples remain literal. Requires salience.write when directives are present; inspect valuations for partial failures.

Needs artifacts.read and wires.write beside documents.write.crdt, and artifacts.write for the path form.

tools.name: create_wires
tools.description: Create one or more local semantic wires in the graph, through its CRDT surface. The predicate is one of: grounds, requires, enables, exemplifies, supports, contradicts, qualifies, flowsInto, produces, intensifiesWith, contains, precedes, consequenceOf, relatedTo (list_wire_predicates gives their meanings); any other name refuses the whole call, and a wire with no predicate is relatedTo. Choose the most specific one that fits. A wire to an artifact may name a region of it: region as the short form L10-L20 (lines, 1-based inclusive), p12 (pdf page), b100-200 (bytes, end exclusive), m:path/in/zip (member) or j:/pointer (json), or targetRegion as an object; the server reads the region, hashes it and sets fileHash (a client value is ignored); an out-of-range or wrong-kind region refuses the wire. artifactPath (absolute, or relative to one of the graph's roots) in place of a target id finds the referenced record for that file or makes one. The region's text is read through read_artifact with the wire id, never through documents.read.

tools.name: sparql_query_named
tools.description: Run one of a class's CANONICAL named queries (T2 query face, item 11) — byId(subject), currentHeads({asOf?}), lineageOf(subject), countBy(attr) — derived from the class's declared SHACL shape + MaterializationSignature (never a hand-maintained per-class query). Scoping comes from the class's declared store_target ONLY (class_dispatch), so the partitioned-store silent zero is structurally impossible. Membrane-ed classes (e.g. sophia-memory-core): no 'observer' → the shared commons only; with 'observer' → commons ∪ that observer's membrane (RATIFIED default). currentHeads is the one server-authoritative current-head reader — one 'current head' semantics everywhere. Returns {graphId, vocab, class, queryName, variables, rows, warnings?} — a query returning zero rows for a shape reason (wrong scope, undeclared attr, missing subject) always says so in 'warnings' or as a structured rejection, never a bare empty result.

class.description: The class name declared by the vocab's contract (e.g. 'MemoryRecord').

params.description: Query-specific arguments: 'subject' (a full subject IRI — byId, lineageOf), 'asOf' (epoch-millis or ISO-8601 datetime — currentHeads; omitted = the live read), 'attr' (a declared predicate CURIE/local-name/URI — countBy).

observer.description: A per-agent membrane. Default = the shared commons (RATIFIED: no observer ⇒ commons only). Ignored, with a warning, on a class with no observer membrane.

tools.name: emporium_write
tools.description: T-W item 1 — the MCP write surface over the existing spine (I1 gate, SHACL, minting, journal, contested lineage). 'vocab' names ONE registered vocab; 'records' are flat JSON objects with NO 'subject'/'vocab' field (the client never mints identity — Law 2; use 'clientRef' for correlation). Dispatches on the vocab's resolved write_target: 'sophia-memory-core' (a membrane-ed class) routes through the memory lane — records use the SAME camelCase shape 'remember'/'remember_batch' accept (content/scope/kind/contentOrientation/visibility/status/sourceRefs/…) plus per-record 'supersedes'/'contradicts' (Law 3: change is lineage, passed through to the spine's existing supersession machinery — content-hash identity converges on a byte-identical resubmission, outcome 'converged'). Any OTHER registered vocab routes through the generic lane — records use '{kind: <ClassName>, ...predicate fields, localId|clientRef}' (the existing generic-ingest shape); supersedes/contradicts have no machinery there and are REJECTED loudly (a materialize class's only reappearance is a plain resubmission of the same localId/clientRef — the 'Replace'-strategy upsert already performed by the existing subject-scoped reconcile). Law 1 (witnessed or explicitly commons): for a membrane-ed vocab, an observer-less write WITHOUT 'publish: true' is a loud rejection; with 'observer' (top-level, or per-record 'observerAgentId') and no 'publish', the write lands in the writer's OWN membrane; 'publish: true' forces the shared commons (the given observer, if any, is not used for placement — flagged in 'warnings', never silent). A non-membrane vocab has no observer concept — 'publish'/'observer' are accepted as a no-op, flagged in 'warnings'. Law 5: 'dry_run' runs the SAME structural/SHACL validation preview a real apply would (nothing written) and reports the predicted per-record outcome + any violations. Batches are single-vocab (structural) and ALL-OR-HALT: any SHACL/apply failure marks EVERY record 'halted' and carries the shared 'violations' — never a partial write. Returns {graphId, vocab, dryRun, ok, results:[{subject, outcome:'applied'|'converged'|'halted', flags?}], journalRef?, warnings, violations?}.

vocab.description: The vocab name (e.g. 'sophia-memory-core', 'emporium-bookmark'). ONE vocab per call — a per-record 'vocab' key is rejected.

records.description: Memory lane (vocab='sophia-memory-core'): the remember/remember_batch camelCase record shape, plus optional 'supersedes'/'contradicts' (a subject IRI) and 'observerAgentId' (or bare 'observer'). Generic lane (any other vocab): {kind: <ClassName>, ...predicate fields, localId|clientRef}. NEVER include 'subject' (Law 2) or 'vocab' (Law 3 — batches are single-vocab) on any record — both are a loud, whole-batch rejection.

dry_run.description: Default false. true = the SAME structural/SHACL validation preview a real apply would run — NOTHING is written; the response's per-record outcome and 'violations' are the predicted verdict.

publish.description: Default false. For a membrane-ed vocab (Law 1): true forces the shared commons (an explicit publication act); false (the default) requires an 'observer' — an observer-less write without publish=true is a loud rejection. No-op (flagged in 'warnings') for a non-membrane vocab.

observer.description: The writer's own membrane (a per-agent witness id). Default for every record that omits its own 'observerAgentId'. No-op (flagged in 'warnings') for a non-membrane vocab.

operationId.description: Stable source invocation identity. Batched records derive stable child identities from it.

tools.name: emporium_retract
tools.description: T-W item 2, Law 4 (retraction is an event, not an erasure) — mints a retraction EVENT on 'subject' (who/when/rationale) direct-on-store, in whichever named graph the subject already lives in (located by a store-wide scan; this tool takes no vocab/class). Heads exclude it: `sweep::current_heads_by_lineage`/`heads_as_of` — and therefore `sparql_query_named`'s 'currentHeads' — never return a retracted subject as a current (or, for 'as_of', historical) head again. `emporium_read` hides it too. The log keeps it: NO triple is removed — hard-delete stays a SEPARATE, deferred admin-tier act. Re-retracting an already-retracted subject records an ADDITIONAL event (flagged in 'warnings'), never an error. Returns {graphId, subject, graph, kind, rationale, retractedAt, retractionRef, alreadyRetracted, warnings}.

subject.description: A full subject IRI — an existing minted subject the caller read back from a prior write/query (referencing an existing identity is not minting a new one).

rationale.description: Why this subject is being retracted (Law 4: who/when/rationale) — required, non-empty.

observer.description: The witness recording this retraction (attributed via 'retractedBy') — NOT used to locate the subject.

operationId.description: Stable source operation identity. Reuse the same value for an at-least-once retry.

tools.name: sparql_update
tools.description: Run a SPARQL UPDATE against a local graph.

tools.name: rdf_load
tools.description: Load RDF data into a local graph.

tools.name: rdf_dump
tools.description: Dump RDF data from a local graph.

tools.name: list_restore_points
tools.description: List local time-travel restore points for a graph, newest first, with cursor pagination.

tools.name: get_restore_point
tools.description: Read the manifest of a single local restore point, including referenced per-document snapshot ids.

tools.name: create_restore_point
tools.description: Capture a new local restore point bundling the graph's folders and wires with a fresh snapshot of every document. Optional label is shown in listings.

tools.name: diff_restore_points
tools.description: Compute aggregate document and char-level deltas between a restore point and another (or the live graph).

tools.name: delete_restore_point
tools.description: Delete a local restore point and its bundled graph snapshot. Per-document snapshots referenced by other restore points remain.

tools.name: restore_to_restore_point
tools.description: Apply a local restore point: captures an auto-backup, atomically swaps Y.Doc state, rematerializes RDF, verifies, and on any failure rolls back from the auto-backup. Blocks all CRDT writes for the duration. Returns an operationId for status polling. Pass dryRun=true to validate without applying.

tools.name: get_restore_operation
tools.description: Read the current state of a restore operation: phase, progress, backup pointer, error if any.

tools.name: cancel_restore_operation
tools.description: Request cancellation of an in-flight restore. Cooperatively checked between phases; if cancelled mid-restore, the auto-backup is rolled back so the graph returns to its pre-restore state.

tools.name: read_artifact
tools.description: Perceive a stored artifact and its record (mode, sha256, light index): image kinds return base64 bytes (the agent's vision model can then see it); text returns one page of decoded text (offset and max_chars, default 65536, with nextOffset and totalChars); others return metadata. With wire_id: read the region that wire names on its artifact, now, beside what was stored when it was wired: stale { file, region } with both hashes, regionText (paged), and when the lines moved a re-anchor by the stored text (reanchored { start, end }, or ambiguous with candidates, or anchorLost). With region (short form or object) and artifact_id: read that region now, nothing stored. Every answer carries localPath, where the bytes are on this computer (a reference's own file, or the original under the graph's store), so an agent whose harness can read files may open it directly.

wire_id.description: A wire to an artifact; its region is read and judged against the side store.

region.description: Region of the target artifact: short form (L10-L20, p12, b100-200, m:path, j:/pointer) or { kind, ... }.

tools.name: list_artifact_kinds
tools.description: List artifact kinds and their capabilities (perceive/render/derive) from the graph-native kind ontology.

tools.name: list_artifact_revisions
tools.description: List the version history (revisions) of an artifact, newest first.

tools.name: restore_artifact_revision
tools.description: Restore an artifact to a prior revision (checkpoints the current state first, so it is reversible).

tools.name: source_pull
tools.description: Pull one identity-fenced, complete source bundle for a graph. The bundle includes the graph's and its documents' Y.Docs, Meaningful Object current-state and event sources, memory, valuations, retractions, conflicts, receipts, and the source contract registry. Persist the whole bundle and its complete manifest atomically before claiming offline completeness.

graphIncarnation.description: Optional on first pull; required on subsequent pulls to reject a replacement graph.

expectedRevision.description: Staleness guard (chronicle): the document revision you last read. The write is refused with a revision conflict if the document has changed since; re-read, or pass force=true.

force.description: Bypass the expectedRevision staleness guard explicitly. The override is recorded on the document's chronicle (lastForcedAt / lastForcedBy) — possible, never silent.

agent.description: Name of the agent making this write (e.g. beta). Recorded as the document's updatedBy / createdBy in the chronicle; the credential it rides on is kept as provenance. Omit for a human owner write.

tools.name: source_push
tools.description: Atomically accept a batch of stable, identity-fenced offline source intents, return durable idempotency receipts, and materialize their effects. Current-state Meaningful Objects use causal base versions and explicit conflicts; event sources use stable event identity; Y.Doc updates merge; lifecycle effects are resumable.

tools.name: source_rebuild
tools.description: Recompute disposable Meaningful Object, memory, valuation, retraction, conflict, and workflow projections from the identity-fenced durable source ledger, reporting source and projection set hashes for rebuild verification.
